withdrawn_reason: The join is UNVALIDATED and engine/rollout_r1_join.py says so itself. Phase 1 walks the INGESTED corpus and counts all four brought Pokemon off an open sheet; porygon2.py parses a public log and can only count what has appeared. Rows join on game id and turn index, and the continuous HP witness rejects the result: on the rows alive_diff admitted, the two sides' summed HP correlates at 0.118 and only ~7% agree within half a percent of one HP bar. 230 of 9,201 rows survive both witnesses, and those survivors are the early quiet turns where every judge sits near a coin. The cause is definitional, not a bad join key, so it is not fixable by choosing a better key.
renamed_why: This file kept the name of the R1 gate, and engine/status.js read it and printed a WITHDRAWN result as R1's status for a day. A withdrawn result must stay readable — CLAUDE.md forbids silently rewriting a prior conclusion — but it must never be the file a gate reads. The R1 gate name now belongs to the recomputed result in data/rollout-r1.json; this keeps its numbers verbatim under a name that says what it is.
do_not_quote: No number below is a result. They are recorded so the withdrawal can be checked rather than believed.
caveat: Positions are the ones phase 1 sampled, joined by game id and turn index and checked with an independently computed alive_diff. Rows whose witness disagreed were dropped, not forced.
note_on_the_keys: The `porygon3` keys are verbatim from the 2026-08-03 run. The current engine/rollout_r1_join.py writes `porygon2`; the committed file predates that rename. Preserved rather than corrected, because correcting a withdrawn artifact's field names would make it look regenerated when it was not.
note_on_the_row_count: 230 joined + 7,007 dropped = 7,237, not 9,201. The remaining rows found no candidate on the porygon2 side at all and were never offered to the witness. That the join reached only 79% of the dump is itself part of the withdrawal.
